newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: INL says NZ Sky takeover talks on track.
newsitem.headline: INL says NZ Sky takeover talks on track.

text.p: Independent Newspapers Ltd said on Thursday talks to buy a controlling stake in New Zealand pay television operator Sky Television remained on track.
INL is about half-owned by Australia's News Corp.

Managing director Mike Robson told the New Zealand Press Association that negotiations for the purchase of the U.S.-owned HKP Partnership's 51 percent holding in Sky were proceeding satisfactorily "and we are hoping to conclude them as soon as we possibly can".

INL revealed it was in talks to buy the stake from HKP just over a week ago. HKP's owners include Time Warner, TCI Communications, Ameritech and Bell Atlantic, telecoms companies which each have a stake in Telecom Corp of New Zealand Ltd.
Meanwhile, The New Zealand Herald newspaper reported that Sky Network Television made a net loss of NZ$20.6 million in 1996, more than twice its 1995 deficit of $9.8 million.

The paper quoted Sky's chief financial officer Paul Smart as saying the net loss reflected the continuing early overheads since start-up in 1990, and that in the meantime the company looked to its EBITDA performance which had shown an increase in earnings since 1994 to $40.9 million from $13.9 million.
Smart would not say when Sky expected to break even at net level, however, saying only it was "on the horizon".
Sky's revenue from subscribers and advertising has almost doubled over the past two years, from $77 million in 1994 to $132 million last year.
Smart said he believed Sky had now signed up enough subscribers to achieve critical mass. One in three New Zealand homes buys the service which has aboiut 300,000 subscribers.
Sky's other main shareholders are state-owned TVNZ (16.3 percent), Heatley Jarvis Investments (15.8 percent), Todd Corporation (8.8 percent), and Tappenden Group (7.7 percent).
